title: Revert Governor: simulated-load rollback decision engine with economic fallbacks
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a 'Revert Governor' — an automated decision engine that can safely revert risky config changes by running fast simulated-load trials and an economic impact predictor before triggering automated rollback. This reduces noisy manual rollbacks and prevents sustained cost regressions caused by config updates (batching, cache TTLs, kernel flags). The governor must integrate with our existing apply pipeline, preflight simulator, and rollout orchestration, and expose clear signals in Console for operator overrides.
background_and_rationale: We frequently see config rollouts that increase per-token cost or latency due to subtle interactions with batching and KV cache behavior. Existing heuristics are brittle: either overly conservative (delaying rollouts) or too aggressive (triggering false rollbacks). The Revert Governor combines three components: 1) lightweight simulated-load execution of the new config on a shadow pool, 2) a cost/latency impact predictor trained on historical telemetry and batching profiles, and 3) a conservative decision policy with multiple guardrails (stability windows, confidence thresholds, and staged quarantine of KV cache state). This project is a complement to the batching/caching recommender — it acts as a last-resort safety net when automated tuning is applied or manual config changes are rolled out.
acceptance_criteria: Governor evaluates a config change in preflight and returns a deterministic pass/fail plus confidence score
Simulated-load runs reproduce 90% of production request patterns for targeted routes (sampling config) within a 5-minute window
Automatic rollback triggers only when confidence > 80% that the change causes median latency regression > 20ms or per-token cost increase > 6% for a sustained 3-minute window
Rollback action includes a state reconciliation step to rehydrate safe KV cache prefixes or gracefully flush and warm caches to avoid cold-start spikes
Operators can opt-out per-release via a Console toggle and can manually approve a revert within a 10-minute grace window
All decisions and telemetry are recorded and visible in Console (change timeline, simulation artifacts, and PR link)
design_decisions: Run simulated-load in an isolated shadow pool to avoid user-impact; reuse existing dedicated simulation cluster (sim-cluster-1)
Use an ensemble predictor: a lightweight cost model (rules + linear regression) for fast decisions and a longer historical model for retrospective analysis
Implement a three-tier guardrail: soft alert (notify), automated canary rollback (staged), full rollback (automatic) depending on severity and confidence
Quarantine policy: when KV cache divergence suspected, mark affected prefixes as quarantined and perform incremental rewarm to the prior state to avoid cascading latency spikes
Decision transparency: every automated revert emits a rationale blob (predicted delta, sampled traces, simulation config) persisted in the changelog
implementation_tasks: Wire preflight hook into change-apply pipeline to schedule a simulated-load job with the proposed config
Add cost/latency predictor service endpoint (predictor.redwood.svc) that accepts sample traces and returns a delta + confidence
Implement governor decision engine as a new microservice (revert-governor) with a pluggable policy DSL
Extend rollout controller to accept governor actions (recommend, canary-revert, auto-revert) and expose operator overrides
KV cache quarantine: add prefix tagging and rewarm API to serving runtime + reconcile script that runs post-revert
Console: new change timeline card showing simulation outcome, predicted impact, and one-click rollback history
End-to-end e2e test harness: simulate config application, run governor, assert safe fallback and no functional regressions
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary 2/10 routes): deploy revert-governor in read-only mode to collect simulation signals (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (soft automation): enable 'recommend' actions for a subset of internal releases (1 week)
Phase 3 (staged rollback): enable canary rollback for non-critical tenants with auto-revert policy (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (full): enable auto-revert with operator opt-out by default for all hosted tenants (after security review and e2e pass)
Backout: rollback feature gate if false positive rate > 5% over a 48-hour window
telemetry_and_signals: Per-route median and p95 latency pre/post change
Per-token cost estimate: token counts * model unit price adjusted by batching efficiency multiplier
Batch size distribution shift (mean, stddev) and caching hit-rate delta
KV cache miss spikes and cold-start counts correlated with prefix lists
Model fallback frequency (when routing falls back to cheaper model variants)
Synthetic-sim results: simulated request success rate and latency histogram
simulation_results_summary: Initial dry-run on sim-cluster-1 (2025-02-20) with a subset of changes (cache_ttl=14->7s) produced a predicted 8.3% per-token cost increase driven by reduced cache hit-rate; median latency increased by 18ms. Predictor confidence 87%. Governor in recommend-only mode raised an alert and created a remediation suggestion (increase batching window). No automatic revert executed.

open_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives could cause unnecessary reverts and customer-facing regressions. Mitigation: require high confidence threshold and staged canaries before full auto-revert.
Risk: KV cache quarantine may force large rewarms that saturate backend. Mitigation: incremental rewarm with rate-limiter and sample-based warmup.
Risk: Predictor model drift over time. Mitigation: daily retraining job and backtesting with sliding window of telemetry.
Risk: Simulation not representative of long-tail routes. Mitigation: improve sample selection and include tail-route fuzzing in e2e harness.
